title: Others keep Thomas: ‘vow’ analogically covers God-promises and Saint-promises—absolute vs relative
source_text: XXXII. Alii vero facilius se explicant, a doctrina Thomae non recedentes, in qua fatetur votum de sola promissione Deo facta dici; verum ex usu Ecclesiae. Juxta quem, votum est nomen quoddam generale quod analogice dicitur de promissione facta Deo & Sanctis. Inter quae vota alii hoc discrimen constituunt, quod votum Deo factum sit absolutum, illud vero quod fit Sanctis relativum: nimirum quia licet ad Sanctos, ut jam dictum, quodammodo terminetur, ultimo tamen ad Dei gloriam refertur.
pass_a_gloss: But others explain themselves more easily, not departing from Thomas’s doctrine, in which he confesses that a vow is said of a promise made to God alone; yet from the use of the Church. According to which, vow is a certain general name which is said analogically of a promise made to God and to the Saints. Among which vows others constitute this distinction, that a vow made to God is absolute, but that which is made to the Saints is relative: namely because although it is terminated in a certain way on the Saints, as already said, yet ultimately it is referred to the glory of God.
pass_b_english: Another School path: Church usage stretches ‘vow’ analogically to Saint-promises.
God-vows absolute; Saint-vows relative—ending finally in God’s glory.

choices.english: from the use of the Church
choices.why: Usage widens ‘vow’ beyond Thomas’s strict God-only sense.
